proposals.text: Proposal: Shift next cycle's research from entry-side skip mining (gen21's five-flag combo was rejected with loss_removal_efficiency 0.0 — that vein is exhausted) to exit management, using `exit_research` on a registered ExperimentRegistry replay of the sealed holdout. Measured evidence: in outcome_learning.json (n=2,517), TP closes earn +0.107 expectancy (net +47.80) while the bot's own manual/flatten closes (quick_win 1,383, never_green 1,288) number 1,927 at -0.0135 expectancy (net -26.07), with payoff ratio 0.34 against a 74.6% breakeven WR and SL hits averaging -0.55 (~5x an average win). Falsifiable hypothesis: replacing quick_win/never_green early-flattening with hold-to-original-TP/SL on the identical trade population flips net expectancy from -0.012 to >0 without raising tail_loss_5pct beyond -0.6 or daily-loss halt frequency. Test offline first (no code/champion changes, demo-only shadow decisions logged as usual); the candidate promotes only if every gate in promote.py passes — OOS E strictly >0 and full-$ PnL strictly beats the live five-flag combo — otherwise it is recorded as rejected like gen21. This follows the corpus principle in *Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom* (Van Tharp) that expectancy is set by exit asymmetry, not win rate, which this system currently violates.

question: The AEGIS MT5 DEMO bot is running the intelligent firehose with the validated-state gate. Given the current measured evidence, identify ONE concrete, falsifiable improvement candidate for the next research cycle. Do not modify code or the champion. Cite book corpus passages if relevant.
